macro: Markets enter this week focused on the Fed's September 15-16 FOMC meeting, where CME FedWatch pricing puts the odds of a 25-basis-point hike near 90% — the central bank's first increase since July 2023, after a hold-then-cut cycle brought the target range down to 3.50%-3.75% by late 2025. August CPI held core inflation at a 2.4% annual pace even as headline CPI ran at 3.4%, with Middle East supply disruptions keeping energy costs elevated. Retail sales, jobless claims, housing starts, and industrial production all land this week and will color how the Fed frames its projections. The single most important date to watch: Wednesday, September 16, 2026, 2:00 p.m. ET, when the FOMC releases its rate decision and updated Summary of Economic Projections.
btc_status: Bitcoin trades near $77,200, still roughly 20% above its 200-week moving average of about $63,770, after pulling back from a $79,890 high on September 12 as Fed rate-hike odds climbed. Today's Crypto Fear & Greed Index reading is data unavailable; the level to watch is the $75,000 support zone that has held through the past week's pullback.

energy: WTI crude traded near $102.52 a barrel, up about 2.5% on the session, while Brent settled around $104 after briefly testing near $110 intraweek — a nearly 9% weekly gain before Friday's pullback. The EIA's most recent Weekly Petroleum Status Report (week ended September 4, 2026) showed commercial crude inventories fell 0.4 million barrels, close to the five-year average for this time of year. Supply risk stays elevated: Houthi forces seized the Yemeni port of Mocha near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait this week, and Saudi Arabia briefly shut a cross-country pipeline after attacks on its energy infrastructure.
vix_and_dollar: The VIX closed at 15.84 on September 11, 2026 — down more than 11% on the day and squarely in the 'normal' 15-20 range — even as the dollar index (DXY) extended a third straight session of gains to trade near 99.1. Calm equity volatility alongside a firming dollar into the Fed decision suggests risk appetite is intact but investors aren't yet positioning for a surprise.
mortgage_rate: The 30-year fixed mortgage rate averaged 6.76% for the week of September 10, 2026, up from 6.71% the week prior, per Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey. Higher borrowing costs continue to weigh on purchase activity even as inventory improves, keeping affordability the binding constraint for buyers.
personal_finance_deep_dive: Bankrate's 2026 Annual Emergency Savings Report found 59% of Americans couldn't cover a $1,000 emergency expense without borrowing — only 30% said they'd pay from savings outright, while a third said they'd have to go into debt. The gap concentrates among lower- and middle-income households already stretched by a personal savings rate near multi-year lows and credit card balances near record highs. It signals a household sector with little buffer heading into a week where a Fed rate hike could raise borrowing costs further rather than ease them.
wealth_building_deep_dive: Morningstar's Annual US Fund Fee Study shows the asset-weighted average fund fee has fallen to 0.34% from 0.83% two decades ago, with many broad index funds and ETFs now charging under 0.05%. That gap compounds: on a $500 monthly contribution over 30 years, cutting fees from 0.83% to 0.05% can add tens of thousands of dollars to a final balance purely from lower cost, with no added risk. A concrete step worth taking this week: pull up your 401(k) or brokerage statement and confirm the expense ratio on your largest holding is under 0.10%.
